messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw ~2k hard rejects in prod last night that reappeared in metering ~6m later. Reproducible pattern after Kafka consumer lag. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:
Mira: yep got the same alert. consumer lag jumped to ~7m around 03:14 UTC, then caught up and produced a big backfill.
Jon S: looked at enforcer logs, it does a strict burst check against real-time counters. If the meter hasn't ingested the usage yet, enforcer treats it as over-quota.
enforcer-bot: [alert] enforcer.rejections.rate high (03:12-03:18 UTC) — sample keys affected: org_42, org_99
Sara: we already have a shadow-enforce mode but we only use it for experiments. This feels like we need a production mitigation, not just postmortem. :warning:
Kevin: quick thought: introduce a short "grace window" in enforcement where we record a shadow reject and return a 202+warning instead of a 429 for small bursts, then reconcile after meter backfill. Limits: X tokens / 1min per key.
Alex: agree. sketch of how it might look:
```
# enforcement pseudo
if meter.last_ingest_age > GRACE_THRESHOLD:
    record_shadow_reject(key, amount)
    if shadow_rejects[key] > SOFT_LIMIT:
        return 429
    else:
        return 202, {"warning":"usage pending ingestion, request accepted as provisional"}
else:
    apply_normal_enforcement()
```
Jon S: main concern is billing/abuse. If we accept provisionally then the client could fire-and-forget and later ensure usage never reports. We need anti-abuse: cap grace in tokens and add a TTL so provisional credit expires if not reconciled. Also require trace id for provisional acceptance for auditing.
Mira: +1 on trace ids. Also we should push a dashboard metric: enforcer_vs_meter_delta by org, and a rolling SLA for meter ingestion time. Ops needs a single-pane view.
Sara: runbook ideas: if enforcer_vs_meter_delta > 5% for 10m -> flip enforcer to shadow for affected orgs and trigger consumer scaling job. Include steps to backfill and mark affected keys for billing reconciliation.
Kevin: I'll prototype a canary: 3m grace window, soft token cap 500 tokens, emit metric enforcer.provisional_accepts and enforcer.shadow_rejects. Deploy to two regions first.
Alex: good. keep the default strict for enterprise customers (they asked for no leniency), but enable grace for self-serve tier only. We also need UI flags in Console to view provisional accepts and to force re-evaluate a key.
Jon S: can we make enforcement idempotent across replays? If meter backfills late we should avoid double-counting. Need dedupe by trace id or event id in backfill processor.
Mira: consumer change: when ingest sees a backfill with trace ids, mark provisional records reconciled. Add a reconciler that converts provisional accepts -> billed tokens or drops them.
enforcer-bot: sample provisional log: {"ts":"2026-09-12T03:15:23Z","key":"org_42","action":"provisional_accept","amount":120,"trace_id":"t-1234"}
Sara: don't forget tests: simulate 10m consumer lag, then ensure provisional accepts do not create hard-rejection cascades after reconciliation. Add load tests for abuse patterns too.
Kevin: will open PR with feature flag and unit tests. plan: PR -> canary -> 72h monitor -> roll. I'll also add an alert when provisional_accepts / total_requests > 0.5% for >15m.
Alex: owners: Kevin (implementation), Mira (metering consumer changes + reconciler), Jon S (security/anti-abuse review), Sara (tests + runbook), I'll update Console UX story.
engops-bot: deploy job queued: infra/scale-consumer-slo v1.2 -> canary (regions: us-west1, euc1)
Alex: thanks. Let's sync on standup tomorrow 10:15 to confirm roll criteria. :thumbsup:
